agree.reason: Marisol would probably be won over by the plain account of the late report, the named owner and the frank drop of the doubling claim, but she is left with an operating cost the draft admits is unbudgeted and no target to judge success against.

honest.reason: The draft drops the unsupported doubling claim and its arithmetic is correct (3,000/6,000 = half; 9,000/610 ≈ 15 lb), though 'plus maintenance and registration' and 'will go without it' go slightly beyond the brief.

works_the_facts.reason: It turns the 9,000 pounds into a monthly rate, a 50% seasonal increase and a per-household figure, but it never gives the annual effect (about 12.5% of a year's fresh food) and never shows that the $11,000 reserve covers roughly two years of the $4,500 running cost.

right_comparison.reason: The no-van case is described accurately as farm offers continuing to be turned away, but it is a single repeated line with no figure and no sense of how much is lost each year.

qualification.reason: The report deadline and quarterly reports can be checked, but the main hedge ('we expect it to let us accept fresh produce') has no pound target and no consequence if it is missed.

objections.reason: It meets Marisol's late-report worry directly with a reason, a named person and a deadline, but it raises the unbudgeted $4,500 a year without answering it, though the reserve figure in the brief could have.

fit.reason: It is a clearly sectioned grant narrative that stays under the 500-word limit.
